subject: Revised MBTA Bus Network Redesign Plan
overview: The MBTA presented a revised bus network redesign proposal that restores several local routes and one-seat rides following over 20,000 public comments. Officials apologized for technical issues that prevented many residents from attending and announced a future follow-up meeting to ensure comprehensive community feedback.

items.title: Title VI and Meeting Procedures
items.summary: Moderators reviewed non-discrimination policies and provided instructions for ASL, Spanish, and Mandarin interpretation services.

items.title: MBTA Bus Transformation Vision
items.summary: Officials outlined the project goal to increase total service by 25% across the region to better reflect post-pandemic travel needs and prioritize equity for transit-dependent populations.

items.title: Revised Network Overview
items.summary: The MBTA revised two-thirds of the initial draft routes to restore service to medical facilities, reduce walking distances for seniors, and preserve one-seat rides like the Route 39 to Copley.

items.title: Implementation Phasing and Infrastructure
items.summary: The new network will be phased in over five years starting in 2023, contingent on bus operator hiring and the construction of accessible stops and transit priority signals.

items.title: Regional Breakout for Medford and Surrounding Areas
items.summary: Service planners detailed Medford-area changes, including the restoration of the 89 and 354 routes and the realignment of the T96 to maintain service on High Street and Winthrop Street.

items.title: Public Comment and Technical Capacity Issues
items.summary: Elected officials and residents raised concerns about specific route frequencies, the removal of the Danvers Square loop, and the exclusion of constituents due to a 300-person Zoom capacity limit. The MBTA stated it would schedule a follow-up meeting to allow more public participation.
